claims.text: Elemental Cr films on zirconium-alloy cladding suffer from Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes accelerated degradation and premature failure of elemental Cr coatings.
A thin TiN interlayer will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion between the Cr coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion with a TiN interlayer will preserve coating integrity.
The TiN interlayer will enhance Cr-coating durability under both subcritical-water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam conditions.
ALD or PVD can produce a uniform, dense, approximately 100 nm TiN barrier on the zirconium-alloy surface.
A dense TiN barrier physically impedes atomic transport between the Cr coating and zirconium-alloy substrate.
Suppressing interfacial transport with TiN will preserve the oxidation-resistant behavior of the elemental Cr layer.
TiN-interlayered samples will have lower interfacial diffusion rates than unmodified Cr-coated samples.
TiN-interlayered samples will exhibit reduced oxidation kinetics relative to unmodified Cr-coated samples.
TiN-interlayered samples will exhibit improved mechanical coating integrity relative to unmodified Cr-coated samples.
Approximately 350°C water exposure for hundreds of hours is an applicable subcritical-water service regime for evaluating the coating.
Approximately 1000°C steam exposure for minutes to one hour is an applicable accident-relevant regime for evaluating the coating.
Elemental Cr-coated zirconium-alloy cladding provides good protection but undergoes accelerated degradation from Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperature.
